recipes: Hyderabadi Chicken Biriyani: Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili, mint, coriander, and fried onions. Layer with 70% cooked basmati rice, saffron milk, and ghee, then cook on dum until the chicken finishes gently under the rice.

Kolkata Biriyani: Build a lighter spiced base with meat, potato, and subtle aromatics like kewra and rose water. Layer with rice and cook covered so the perfume stays delicate rather than aggressively masala-heavy.

Thalassery Biriyani: Use short-grain kaima rice instead of basmati. Cook the masala and rice separately, layer with fried onions, nuts, and raisins, then finish on low heat for a sweeter Malabar profile.

Ambur Style Biriyani: Keep the masala compact and peppery with dried red chilies, curd, and mint. The rice is usually seeraga samba, which absorbs flavor quickly and gives a more compact, restaurant-style texture.

Vegetable Dum Biriyani: Roast paneer or mixed vegetables lightly first so they hold shape. Use browned onions, mint, coriander, and whole spices between rice layers, then steam until the grains finish fluffy and fragrant.
